name: Forward Walking Lunges — Barbell
description: Barbell walking lunges are a compound unilateral exercise performed with a barbell across the upper traps. The lifter steps forward continuously, alternating legs for a set distance or rep count. The barbell adds significantly more load than dumbbells and challenges core stability and balance throughout the movement. The alternating nature trains dynamic single-leg strength and hip flexor flexibility.

execution.starting_position: Unrack the barbell from a power rack and position it across the upper traps (similar to a high-bar squat). Stand with feet hip-width apart at the edge of an open space.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the barbell at an appropriate weight — significantly less than a barbell squat. Ensure you have enough open floor space for the number of lunges planned.
steps: Step 1: Step one foot forward into a lunge stance, bending both knees simultaneously.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee to near the floor while keeping the front shin nearly vertical.
Step 3: Drive through the front heel to bring the rear foot forward past the front foot, completing one step.
Step 4: Immediately step the new leading foot forward and repeat on the opposite side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe rhythmically — exhale on each drive up.
common_mistakes: Step length too short, causing the front shin to angle too far forward
Leaning the torso to one side under barbell load
Rear knee crashing to the floor
safety_considerations: Requires open floor space — ensure the path is clear
High demand on balance with a barbell — develop with dumbbells first
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee to approximately 1-2 inches from the floor each step.
coaching_cues: Rear knee drops, don't crash it
